subject: Hybrid index routing & governance for Pinecone fallthrough
messages:
From: Claire Huang <claire@pinecone.io>
To: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
Cc: ethan@blueridge-analytics.com
Date: Sat, 01 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Intro: hybrid index routing / S3 fallthrough scenario

Vanessa — thanks for the quick sync last week. As discussed, Pinecone has a cohort of customers asking for a documented pattern for 'hot vector store + cold object store' fallthrough with an orchestration layer that supports:
- deterministic routing by vector index shard / namespace
- automated S3 fallthrough for cold retrievals (pointer-based)
- clear encryption and residency controls for regulated data

Ethan from BlueRidge will help sketch an ops playbook and governance checklist; our ask is whether Redwood will accept a route-level policy that can: 1) prefer Pinecone for latency-critical queries and 2) automatically redirect to S3 + pgvector fallback when match score is below threshold or cost-saver mode is enabled.

Can you confirm Redwood's compatibility constraints (model of routing policy config, expected TLs for fallthrough, and any tagging/metadata you require)? Attaching a short PoC diagram.

—Claire

Attachment: hybrid-routing-diagram.v1.png (image/png, 420KB)

From: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
To: Claire Huang <claire@pinecone.io>, Ethan Lowe <ethan@blueridge-analytics.com>
Cc: sergio_alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 03 May 2027 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intro: hybrid index routing / S3 fallthrough scenario

Hi Claire / Ethan — looping our partnerships and partner-eng team so we can align on both the technical pattern and GTM touchpoints. Quick answers:

- Redwood can express per-route fallback policies today (policy language: route.policy.fallback = [modelVariant|vectorStore|externalFetch]). We can add a vector-store-first, s3-fallback template.
- Latency SLOs: prefer <50ms p95 for Pinecone-served hits; fallthrough will typically add 200–400ms depending on object size and pgvector re-index step.
- We require object pointers be signed URLs or KMS-encrypted pointers; we cannot accept plaintext S3 object keys in metadata.

Next steps I propose: BlueRidge and Pinecone build a short ops/governance checklist (2 pages) + a 2-week PoC plan. Sergio/Marissa — can you take the lead on acceptance criteria and commercial implications? I attached a baseline governance checklist template for internal review.

Thanks,
Vanessa

Attachment: governance-checklist.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet, 58KB)

From: sergio_alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Claire Huang <claire@pinecone.io>, Ethan Lowe <ethan@blueridge-analytics.com>
Date: Tue, 04 May 2027 11:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intro: hybrid index routing / S3 fallthrough scenario

Vanessa / team — thanks. Commercial notes from my side:
- If Pinecone is the primary, we need to agree SLIs for retrieval accuracy and latency for the first 90 days of the pilot. SLAs beyond pilot may impact Dedicated capacity commitments.
- Pricing: recommend a credit share model for PoC (Redwood covers platform/runtime, Pinecone subsidizes per-query vector cost for first 10k queries, customer covers storage).
- Contract redlines: data residency and indemnity language must reference our standard partner addendum.

Action items I propose:
1) BlueRidge to draft acceptance criteria (tech + ops).
2) Claire to confirm per-query credit commit for PoC.
3) Marissa/Vanessa to produce a one-pager for GTM positioning.

I'll draft a short term-sheet and loop legal after we have Claire's confirmation.

Sergio

Team — attached is BlueRidge's recommended acceptance checklist and a short ops-runbook (2 pages) that maps:
- When to trigger fallthrough (score threshold + cache-miss patterns)
- How to materialize pointers into pgvector for subsequent fast reads (async ingestion window and TTL choices)
- Audit events to emit to Redwood Console for lineage and cost tracking

A few calls out:
- For regulated accounts we'll enforce object encryption with customer-managed keys; BlueRidge can add a verification job in the PoC.
- For cost control, enable a 'warm-up' window where the first N hits repopulate the vector store before full fallthrough is applied.

From: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 05 May 2027 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intro: hybrid index routing / S3 fallthrough scenario

All — this is great. Decisions / summary (finalizing for PoC kickoff):
1) Pilot scope: 30-day PoC with one joint customer (EastMed Health) to validate latency, cost, and governance controls.
2) Acceptance criteria (short): p95 latency for Pinecone <= 60ms when served; fallthrough path end-to-end <= 600ms for 95% of requests; audited pointer access with KMS keys.
3) Commercials: Pinecone to provide 10k credits; Redwood to waive platform runtime fees for PoC; customer pays S3/storage. Sergio will circulate term-sheet draft by Thu EOD.
4) Ops: BlueRidge to run initial checklist + runbook; Redwood will add route.policy template and an event set to Console for cost attribution.

Please review and reply with any blockers. If no objections, I'll post the DocuSign PoC acceptance form and kick off on Monday, May 10.

Thanks — Vanessa
